title: IS12:: fahr_input.c (3.4)

lines.code: float fahr; /* the temperature to be converted */
lines.explanation: This is the variable that has to get the value from user's input. It is declared with no initialization since we do not know it's value yet.
This empty line separates declarations from executable statements
This comment explains the purpose of the following section of the code

This printf statement prints the prompt to the user (to hint that the input is expected). Note that there is no 
 at the end of the string - we want the cursor to stay at the same line
This scanf statement will read a string entered by the user, interpret it as a floating point number (following %f specification) and put the converted floating point value into variable fahr
This empty line separates two sections of the code and makes the code structure more clear
This comment explains the purpose of the following section of the code
printf command is often split into several lines, but the text inside "" stays on the same line!

The values to be printed are the value of farh (temperature in Fahrenheit entered by the user) and the corresponding temperature in Celsius calculated with the formula. Both values are printed using %6.2 specification
